title: RideFlow
description: A ride-hailing backend simulation exploring service boundaries, authentication, and location updates.
results: The repository contains gateway and service integration tests alongside application code.
Authentication event contracts and service boundaries are available for inspection.
proof: Separate gateway, authentication, user, driver, and location services.
context: RideFlow explores how a ride-hailing backend can be split into services. The current repository contains gateway, authentication, user, driver, and location services; it is a simulation, not a commercial ride-hailing operation.
contribution: Implemented service boundaries, authentication flows, gateway routing, and location-related backend work in a TypeScript/NestJS workspace.

architecture.summary: The gateway fronts separate backend services. Service code separates application use cases, domain interfaces, and infrastructure integrations.

components.name: API gateway
components.detail: Routing, JWT middleware, and request throttling.

components.name: Domain services
components.detail: Authentication, user, driver, and location responsibilities.

decisions.title: Separate entry points from domain work
decisions.description: The gateway handles shared request concerns while service modules own their application behavior. This makes boundaries explicit, at the cost of additional routing and operational coordination.

decisions.title: Isolate event publication
decisions.description: An event-publisher interface separates authentication use cases from delivery mechanisms. The repository includes in-memory and Kafka publishers; their presence alone is not evidence of reliable end-to-end event delivery.

decisions.title: Make contracts inspectable
decisions.description: Authentication event documentation specifies payloads and intended consumers. Gateway and service tests provide concrete places to inspect behavior as the simulation develops.

limitations: No production deployment, user adoption, throughput, or fault-tolerance benchmark is claimed. The wider ride-matching and payment vision should not be read as a verified completed system.
resourceNote: Source code is public. No hosted demonstration is listed.
